newsitem.title: UK: "Credible talks" needed for IRA truce - Sinn Fein.
newsitem.headline: "Credible talks" needed for IRA truce - Sinn Fein.

text.p: Sinn Fein accused Britain on Thursday of stalling on key demands that could lead to a new truce by its Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrilla wing.

Sinn Fein, barred from talks because of IRA bomb attacks, signalled that the guerrillas would not declare a ceasefire without a British pledge of a place for republicans in unconditional all-party peace talks.

"Sinn Fein cannot deliver anything unless the British government makes clear that there is to be a credible process of talks, without preconditions, on a broadly acceptable time-frame and with which everyone (can) engage in initiatives to build confidence," senior strategist Martin McGuinness said.
"In short it must be made clear that the British government will not treat any new IRA cessation in the same way that it treated the last one," McGuinness declared.
"Up to now the British government have not made this clear."
McGuinness's comments came against a gloomy climate hanging over the Northern Ireland peace process since February when it was shattered by IRA bombs that ended a 17-month truce.
British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said on Tuesday he saw no prospect of an early IRA truce and that army installations in the province had intensified precautions.

British media reports say the IRA has decided on a strategy of headline-grabbing attacks before a temporary Christmas truce, and that it might soon announce specific terms that it wants from Britain in return for a ceasefire.

Britain says it will take more than "soft words" to prove that any future IRA truce is genuine. Politicians speaking for the province's majority Protestants want London to insist that the IRA hands in weapons before Sinn Fein gets into talks.
Britain, supported by Ireland which is jointly sponsoring current multi-party talks, will not countenance Sinn Fein being admitted until the IRA restores a ceasefire.
